title: Cyrus and the Vow
premise: Bram Thackeray, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter scraping by as a part-time novelist, joins a small-town anonymous pen-pal program to research her next book — only for the organizer's clerical error to pair her with Cyrus Vale, the developer threatening her bakery lease and the son of the man who ruined her family. Writing under assumed names, they fall for each other without knowing it, while in person their rivalry sharpens over the harbor land both claim as inheritance. When identities are revealed at the winter solstice festival, Bram must confront the resentment she carries toward herself for abandoning the lighthouse years ago. She forgives herself, chooses belonging over bitterness, and together she and Cyrus save the bakery and the light, ending with a letter signed with both their real names.
about_author: Paloma Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes love stories set in working harbors, where letters travel slowly and grudges travel slower.

chapters.title: The Last Light on Ledger Row
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram tends the decommissioned lighthouse her grandfather kept, drafting a novel nobody wants while the bakery below faces a lease deadline. Establishes her isolation and her habit of keeping love in past tense. Emotional beat: quiet defiance masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The town librarian launches an anonymous pen-pal program; Bram signs up for character research and receives her first letter from 'C,' witty and needling. She writes back sharper than intended. Emotional beat: reluctant spark of connection.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus Vale arrives to finalize acquisition of the harbor block, including Bram's building, armed with his father's blueprints and his own doubts. He glimpses Bram arguing with his site manager. Emotional beat: ambition curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Enemies at the Counter
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram confronts Cyrus in her bakery; he offers relocation money, she refuses, citing her grandfather's vow to keep the light tended. Their public clash becomes town gossip. Emotional beat: righteous anger with an undertow of attraction.

chapters.title: Letters Unsigned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both write their pen-pal letters after the confrontation, each unknowingly venting about the other to the other. The letters grow tender despite themselves. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus discovers his father's will ties the project to his personal success, revealing the corruption beneath the family fortune. He drinks alone and writes C a confession he doesn't send. Emotional beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Flour and Salt Water
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A storm floods the bakery; Cyrus, inspecting damage, helps sandbag without being asked. Neither mentions the lease. They almost talk like friends. Emotional beat: the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Keeps
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sorting her grandfather's papers, Bram finds her own old rejection letters and the journal entry from the night she left home, blaming everyone but herself. Flashback to her abandonment of the lighthouse. Emotional beat: shame surfacing.

chapters.title: A Proposal in Ink
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus drafts a compromise plan preserving the lighthouse, but his board mocks it; his father's old partner threatens to expose the will's coercion. He burns the midnight oil and one unsent letter too many. Emotional beat: courage meeting institutional rot.

chapters.title: The Pen-Pal Mixer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The library hosts a masked mixer so correspondents can meet anonymously. Bram and Cyrus, both attending on whims, talk for hours without masks slipping — or do they? Each suspects, neither confirms. Emotional beat: intoxicating near-recognition.

chapters.title: Deadline Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The lease expires in thirty days; Cyrus stalls his own board while Bram organizes neighbors. Their sabotage-cum-alliance confuses them both. Letters turn openly romantic. Emotional beat: falling in love twice, in two registers.

chapters.title: The Partner's Leverage
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The father's partner blackmails Cyrus: deliver the demolition or the coerced will goes public, destroying the Vale name. Cyrus considers confessing everything to C instead. Emotional beat: cornered honesty.

chapters.title: Almost Told You
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. On the lighthouse gallery at dusk, Bram nearly tells Cyrus about her pen pal; he nearly tells her about C. An interrupted kiss leaves them both shaking. Emotional beat: longing outrunning fear, then slammed shut.

chapters.title: Signed, Sealed, Mistaken
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The librarian, correcting records, accidentally reveals the pairing error to Bram: her C is Cyrus Vale. Bram rereads every letter and sees him everywhere. She stops writing. Emotional beat: betrayal by coincidence, grief by choice.

chapters.title: Silence on the Line
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus receives no reply and spirals, believing C discovered his identity and rejected him. He signs the demolition order to protect the secret and his name. Emotional beat: self-sabotage dressed as duty.

chapters.title: The Vow Reclaimed
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Facing eviction, Bram reads her grandfather's actual vow aloud: not to keep the light at all costs, but to keep it lit for whoever needs coming home. She realizes she's been guarding a grudge, not a legacy. Emotional beat: reframing inheritance as invitation.

chapters.title: Solstice Festival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the winter solstice festival, the librarian publicly reveals all pairings. Bram and Cyrus stand revealed to each other and to the whole town. He confesses the blackmail and the signed order; she confesses she knew first and said nothing. Emotional beat: mutual exposure, mutual wound.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Alone in the lighthouse, Bram finally forgives the girl who left — writing the forgiveness into her novel's final chapter, then tearing up the eviction notice's power over her heart. She decides to fight for the harbor not against Cyrus but beside him. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness as the story's true climax.

chapters.title: Confession at the Hearing
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the zoning hearing, Cyrus discloses the coerced will and resigns from the board, surrendering his inheritance to break its corruption. His testimony saves the harbor block. Emotional beat: power renounced, integrity claimed.

chapters.title: Relighting
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The town relights the lighthouse; Bram's bakery lease is renewed under a community trust Cyrus helped draft. He waits at the rail with an envelope. Emotional beat: homecoming, literal and emotional.

chapters.title: Yours, Finally Named
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cyrus gives Bram the letter he never sent, now signed with his real name; she answers with one of her own, read aloud on the gallery. First kiss with full knowledge, no masks. Emotional beat: love in present tense at last.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Keeper's Log
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, framed as her published novel's acknowledgments. One year later: the bakery thrives, the light turns nightly, and a new pen-pal season begins — this time with no errors needed. Final line echoes the first letter. Emotional beat: belonging earned and kept.
